questions.problem: Find the principal $9$th root of unity.
questions.worked_solution:
Let $z$ be a $9$th root of unity. This means that 

$$
{z}^{9}=1.
$$

First, we express the complex number $1$ in the form $r{e}^{\text{i}\theta }.$ Notice that $|1|=1$ and $\operatorname{arg}⁡(1)=0.$ Hence, 

$$
1={e}^{\text{i}(0+2k\pi )}={e}^{2k\pi \text{i}},
$$

where $k$ is an integer. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{9}={e}^{2k\pi \text{i}}\,⟹\,z=({e}^{2k\pi \text{i}})^{1/9}={e}^{2k\pi \text{i}/9}.\end{aligned}
$$

The principal root corresponds to $k=1,$ and is therefore equal to ${e}^{2\pi \text{i}/9}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13980994/assets/91eb6ed60e58b03732bdcea3e9858db452d2d998c6a6abed538bbcc76412ed4c.png)

Find the $9$th root of unity highlighted in the diagram above.
questions.worked_solution:
The $n$th roots of unity lie at the vertices of a regular $n$-gon inscribed inside the unit circle in the complex plane. One of the vertices of this regular $n$-gon must lie at the point $(1,0).$

First, we express the complex number $1$ in the form $r{e}^{\text{i}\theta }.$ Notice that $|1|=1$ and $\operatorname{arg}⁡(1)=0.$ Hence, 

$$
1={e}^{\text{i}(0+2k\pi )}={e}^{2k\pi \text{i}},
$$

where $k$ is an integer. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{9}={e}^{2k\pi \text{i}}\,⟹\,z=({e}^{2k\pi \text{i}})^{1/9}={e}^{2k\pi \text{i}/9}.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the index $k$ of our root of unity, we enumerate the roots in the diagram counter-clockwise, starting with the root at $(1,0)$ corresponding to $k=0,$ as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13980994/assets/9b3977b8b51c54a1ef552cff48a3be5a269c92a96742cba5c87e618bb616e5a0.png)

 

So, the required root corresponds to $k=7.$ Substituting this into the expression for roots, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}_{7}={e}^{2(7)\pi \text{i}/9}={e}^{14\pi \text{i}/9}\end{aligned}
$$
